documents.title: Serindit Pay — Merchant Payment Orchestration Platform
Serindit Pay - Merchant Payment Orchestration Platform

constraints.text: Assessment as a PCI DSS v4.0 Level 1 service provider, with the CDE limited to the components listed in Section 12.2.
No sensitive authentication data retained after authorization completes, even if encrypted (PCI DSS v4.0 3.3.1, 3.3.1.2); SAD encrypted while held (3.3.2).
Compliance with SG PDPA 2012, MY PDPA 2010, ID Law 27/2022, TH PDPA 2019 and PH DPA 2012: purpose limitation, retention limits and access logging.
Cascades must never reattempt where card scheme rules prohibit it, and stop at scheme reattempt limits.
Settlement reports published by 09:00 SGT on T+1; Finance says it has confirmed this against merchant contracts.
AWS ap-southeast-1 across three AZs is the primary region, with ap-southeast-3 for DR; the CDE runs in a separate AWS account, VPC and EKS cluster.
Principles override later sections when they conflict.
KYB/onboarding is owned by the Merchant Risk platform; MPOP consumes an approved-merchant event.
The ACQ-PH1 v2 API retires in Q3 2027, so the adapter must migrate to v3 before then.
The first merchant cohort (Singapore, cards and PayNow) goes live after Build Phase 7; other markets follow at four-week intervals.

key_assumptions.text: 2027 volume targets: 10.5 M attempts per day, 2,000 peak TPS, card share 55%, largest merchant 45% of peak (about 900 TPS, marketplace M-0001).
Fewer than 1% of card payments cascade, so the cascade path sits above p99 (Section 21.1). The baseline retryable rate is 3.8%, and the pilot recovered about 31% of retryable outcomes.
Acquirer round-trip p99 is 1,100 ms (2025 production, slowest acquirer). Component p99s sum to 1,338 ms; orchestration overhead is 238 ms.
A DynamoDB global table in default multi-Region eventual consistency mode, with a conditional put on attribute_not_exists(pk), lets exactly one request across regions acquire the lock.
Each idempotency request costs up to 6 WCU, or up to 12,000 WCU table-wide at 2,000 TPS; warm throughput is pre-set to 15,000 WCU before campaigns.
Aurora Global Database lag is typically under one second. Payments in the regional loss window can be recovered from provider status APIs and T+1 reconciliation.
An Aurora spike on db.r7g.8xlarge sustained 2,600 TPS of the full write mix; production uses db.r7g.12xlarge.
Reconciliation finishes about 08:09 SGT at 2027 volume once the last file (ACQ-TH1 at 07:30 SGT) arrives.
One HSM is enough at launch; a second is added when sustained card volume exceeds 1,500 TPS, and daily backups allow re-creation in any AZ.
FRV-1 needs the full PAN for its consortium velocity graph; the Fraud Hook detokenises using the Card Adapter's client library and service role.
Network tokens (VTS/MDES) are the primary card-on-file credential from launch, although the Token Requestor application has not yet been submitted (Backlog item 2).
Several acquirers require the CVC on each cascade re-presentation; incremental and MIT authorizations do not need it.

objectives.text: Give merchants one versioned API across five markets, with rule-based routing and cascading on retryable failures.
Replace five per-market integration stacks with shared routing, one ledger and automated reconciliation.
Support about 15,000 active merchants and a peak of 2,000 payment-creation TPS by the 2027 design target.
One payment, one truth: the payment record and the ledger are the source of truth; provider responses are inputs only.
Card data stays in the Vault: PAN and SAD leave the Vault boundary only over the Card Adapter's connection to an acquirer; all other services handle tokens.
Every mutating call is deduplicated on the pair (merchant, idempotency key).
Money is held as integer minor units with an ISO 4217 code; no floating-point type ever holds an amount.
The ledger is append-only; corrections are new reversing or adjusting journals.
Provider quirks live in adapters; the core never branches on provider identity.
Delivery is at least once and the effect exactly once: consumers deduplicate on stable identifiers.
Fail closed on security; degrade to documented defaults when optional enrichment (fraud signals, BIN metadata) is unavailable.
Least privilege and separation of duties; money-moving permissions are separated from configuration permissions.
Everything is auditable: every mutation, routing decision and admin action can be reconstructed.
Keep PCI DSS scope confined to a small CDE enclave (Vault Edge, Card Vault, CloudHSM, Card Adapter).

intent_summary.statement: MPOP is Serindit Pay's Merchant Payment Orchestration Platform. It accepts merchants' payment requests, routes each one to an acquirer, e-wallet provider or bank-transfer rail, and accounts for every movement of money until the merchant is settled. It replaces five per-market stacks that share no routing or ledger and reconcile by spreadsheet. Its scope is one merchant API across five SEA markets (Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Philippines) for about 15,000 merchants at a peak of 2,000 payment-creation TPS. That scope covers routing, cascading, idempotency, a tokenising card vault, a fraud hook, a double-entry ledger, reconciliation, payouts, webhooks and a merchant admin plane. Dispute case management, KYB, 3DS server internals and lending/BNPL are out of scope.

questions.question: Are the objectives, principles P1-P10, FR/NFR set and Section 24 confirmed decisions stated precisely enough to review against? In particular, does v1.1 consistently carry through its revisions (FR-8, NFR-4, NFR-6, NFR-8, MFA) across Sections 2, 10, 12, 16, 18, 24 and 26?
questions.rationale: The review judges fitness against the design's own requirements and decisions, so any revision that was only partly propagated weakens the baseline.

questions.question: Do the ledger, outbox and balance projector design, and the incremental per-file reconciliation, plausibly meet FR-10, FR-11 and NFR-8 at 2027 volume? Do the worked journal example and the publication timing arithmetic hold?
questions.rationale: These are core objectives (one payment, one truth; daily three-way match); confirming them as strengths is as valuable as finding defects.

questions.question: Does the per-merchant token bucket rate limiting meet NFR-9 when one marketplace merchant is 45% of peak (about 900 TPS)? Do the webhook isolation and SSRF controls meet FR-12 safely?
questions.rationale: Concentration in one merchant makes noisy-neighbour isolation and dispatcher safety material to availability for the other merchants.

questions.question: Are any controls or requirements missing that the objectives need? Candidates: key rotation and HSM key management for the Vault; refunds to customer bank accounts (FR-15), where the nominated account is unverified; API key rotation and revocation; and data-subject handling for the hashed identifiers sent to FRV-1.
questions.rationale: FR-15, NFR-5 and NFR-7 imply controls that the design may not specify.

questions.question: The Redis fast-path key idem:resp:{idempotency_key} has no merchant scope, and a hit returns the stored response without a request-hash check. Does this contradict P3 and FR-5, given that merchants commonly use order IDs as keys? Could it return one merchant's payment object to another merchant, or skip the 422 on body mismatch?
questions.rationale: A key collision across merchants would leak data and break idempotency correctness, which FR-5 and P3 explicitly require.

questions.question: Section 21.1 says fewer than 1% of card payments cascade, but Section 10.5 gives 3.8% retryable outcomes, NFR-2 includes the cascade, and a timeout-triggered cascade alone takes 2,500 ms. Can the cascade path sit above p99? Is the 3DS step accounted for in the latency budget?
questions.rationale: NFR-2 explicitly includes any cascade, and the budget argument rests on a percentage that the design's own baseline contradicts.

queries: DynamoDB global tables conditional writes multi-region eventual consistency last writer wins
DynamoDB global tables multi-region strong consistency MRSC conditional put
DynamoDB global tables ap-southeast-3 availability
questions.question: Under DynamoDB global tables in the default multi-Region eventual consistency mode, is a conditional PutItem with attribute_not_exists evaluated only against the local replica, with conflicting writes in two regions resolved by last-writer-wins? If so, the Section 9.4 claim that exactly one request can acquire the lock regardless of region is false.
questions.rationale: The cross-region deduplication that FR-5 and NFR-4 depend on during failover rests entirely on this claim.

queries: DynamoDB partition throughput limit 1000 WCU 3000 RCU
DynamoDB warm throughput on-demand
DynamoDB global tables replicated write capacity units
questions.question: Are the stated DynamoDB figures correct: per-partition limits of 1,000 WCU and 3,000 RCU, 1 WCU per KB written, and warm throughput pre-setting for on-demand tables? Is replicated write capacity in a global table additional to the 12,000 WCU estimate?
questions.rationale: The capacity sizing in 9.3 and the cost of the global table depend on these limits.

queries: PCI DSS v4.0 requirement 3.3.1.2 card verification code retention after authorization
PCI DSS 4.0 3.3.2 SAD stored electronically prior to completion of authorization
PCI SSC FAQ storing CVV2 for authorization retry
questions.question: Does PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 3.3.1/3.3.1.2 allow the CVC to be retained, encrypted, across cascade re-presentations to different acquirers until the final authorization outcome? Is that cascade window 'before completion of authorization' as Requirement 3.3.2 means it?
questions.rationale: NFR-6 and the confirmed CVC decision depend on this reading of the standard; v1.0's reading was wrong.

questions.question: The Fraud Hook detokenises the PAN using the Card Adapter's library and service role and sends it to FRV-1. Does this contradict P2, the 12.1 rule that only the Card Adapter may detokenise, and the 12.2 classification of the Fraud Hook as out of scope? What does it mean for CDE scope (NFR-5) and for FRV-1 as a third-party service provider?
questions.rationale: An unacknowledged expansion of CDE scope would invalidate the NFR-5 assessment boundary and violates least privilege (P9).

queries: Indonesia Law 27/2022 personal data cross-border transfer requirements
Thailand PDPA section 28 cross-border transfer
Malaysia PDPA 2024 amendment cross-border transfer section 129
questions.question: Do the personal-data flows meet NFR-7 cross-border transfer obligations? These include customer data from all five markets held in Singapore and replicated to Jakarta, and email, phone, device data and PAN sent to FRV-1 while its DPA is still pending.
questions.rationale: NFR-7 names five national laws that each have cross-border transfer conditions; the DR replica and the vendor flow are transfers.

questions.question: Is the merchant admin authentication consistent and complete? Section 18.1 says 'optional TOTP', 18.3 mandates MFA, and the Admin API is meant for automation. How do non-interactive Admin API callers satisfy mandatory MFA and step-up, and what happens to a payout account change when the merchant has only one Owner?
questions.rationale: FR-13 and P8/P9 controls over money-moving actions are only as strong as their unambiguous enforcement.

queries: AWS CloudHSM single HSM availability recommendation multiple AZ
AWS CloudHSM create HSM from backup time
AWS CloudHSM hsm2m operations per second AES unwrap
questions.question: With a single CloudHSM in ap-southeast-1a and uncached DEK unwrap on every detokenise, what happens to card authorizations on loss of that AZ or HSM, and during a regional failover where no HSM or Vault exists in ap-southeast-3? Is this compatible with NFR-3 and NFR-4 (RTO 30 minutes)?
questions.rationale: Every card authorization depends on the HSM, so a single-AZ HSM is a single point of failure for the platform's main revenue path.

queries: Aurora Global Database write forwarding behaviour when primary region unavailable
Aurora Global Database unplanned failover RPO lag managed failover
Aurora global database RPO setting rpo_lag_target
questions.question: Is regional failover workable as written? Write forwarding to the Singapore writer cannot work while Singapore is down; MSK and Redis come back empty; lag-window payments must be found when their attempt records may not have replicated; and the global-table idempotency records may be inconsistent. Can NFR-4's regional RPO and recovery-through-reconciliation be met?
questions.rationale: The v1.1 revision of NFR-4 depends on these recovery paths actually being able to identify every payment in the loss window.

questions.question: Are there unhandled failure paths? Examples: an API pod crashing after the idempotency lock but before the payment is created, so the sweeper has no payment to resolve and the merchant gets 409 for 24 hours; late responses discarded after a cascade has started, which could double-authorize; a late or missing settlement file with no defined handling against the 09:00 SGT deadline; and a settlement line arriving for a payment already PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, where no transition to SETTLED exists.
questions.rationale: FR-2, FR-5, FR-11 and NFR-8 each depend on these edge paths being defined.

questions.question: Which confirmed decisions or 'ready' build phases rest on pending items? Network tokens are confirmed 'from launch' and Phase 3 is marked ready although the TRID application has not been submitted. The first cohort goes live after Phase 7 but the Fraud Hook is Phase 8, while FR-9 requires every card payment to be scored. The FRV-1 DPA is pending.
questions.rationale: Decisions marked confirmed or ready that depend on open items create schedule and compliance exposure at go-live.

queries: Visa reattempt rules category 1 2 3 decline codes limits 30 days
Mastercard merchant advice code 03 21 transaction processing excellence
Visa excessive reattempts response code 05 51 category
questions.question: Are the scheme reattempt rules the Retry Engine relies on (Visa reattempt limits, Mastercard MAC codes, treatment of 05/51) correctly reflected in the outcome classes, especially 51 classified as a final hard decline and 05 as retryable across acquirers?
questions.rationale: FR-7 requires never reattempting where scheme rules prohibit it, and misclassification brings scheme fines.

questions.question: Can each acceptance criterion in Section 26 demonstrate its requirement? For example, the FR-5 test is sequential only, with no concurrent or cross-region duplicates; the NFR-2 test does not specify timeout-class injection; the NFR-4 game day must detect a loss window it cannot observe; the FR-9 test has no review of the PAN flow; and the FR-8 control-slice revert lacks statistical power for small merchants.
questions.rationale: Section 26 is the basis of the Phase 9 test plan, so criteria that cannot catch the failure modes leave requirements unverified.

questions.question: Do the findings preserve or refine the confirmed decisions (idempotency store, single HSM, CVC handling, DR posture, routing thresholds)? Which, if any, warrant an explicit challenge backed by at least two evidence items, for example the global-table cross-region lock claim?
questions.rationale: Approved decisions must be preserved unless strong evidence shows they cannot meet an objective.

questions.question: Are owners, dates and governance decisions assigned for the backlog items, the HSM scale-out trigger, CDE scope changes, fraud fallback risk acceptance (ACCEPT on vendor outage), reconciliation exception handling and DR rehearsal? Is the Section 27 readiness assessment accurate given the findings?
questions.rationale: Without accountable owners, the pending items and risk-acceptance choices the design relies on may not close before go-live.

review_inputs_found: Revision history v1.1 (2026-10-01, page 1) says post-review revisions were made to FR-8; NFR-4, NFR-6 and NFR-8; the idempotency store and cross-region replication (Sections 9, 20, 24); CVC handling (11.2, 12.4); reconciliation scheduling (16.2); merchant authentication and payout account changes (18); and matching acceptance criteria (26).
Title block (page 1) says the document was last updated 2026-10-01 as 'review revisions', which implies a prior review whose findings v1.1 says it addresses.
Section 16.2 (page 13) says Finance has confirmed the 09:00 SGT NFR-8 target against merchant contracts.

Section 27 (pages 21-22) self-assesses the Idempotency Layer, Retry Engine, Card Vault/Card Adapter, Ledger, Payouts and Webhooks as 'Ready', and says the transaction core is specified to implementation level.
Section 28 (page 22) marks Phases 1-3 and 5 as 'No - ready', i.e. not dependent on open design items, including card-on-file with network tokens in Phase 3.
